body: Andorran licence plates are unique in Europe for having an orange dot on the left side.
Andorra only has Generation 2 and 3 coverage. Generation 3 is the most common and the Google car has a visible medium-short antenna.
All Generation 3 coverage was filmed in October, so many trees will have autumn colours.
Andorra has many stone buildings, which can also be found in the nearby French and Spanish Pyrenees.
Andorran snow poles are made of wood and can have various colours.
The main language is Catalan. To distinguish it from Spanish, look for the word 'i' instead of 'y' for 'and'. Catalan is also spoken in eastern Spain.
The Catalan word for street is 'carrer'.
Andorra has kilometre markers with CG and CS road numbers, which can look similar to Spanish ones.
Andorra uses yellow reflectors on its guardrails, a feature only shared with Spain and Belgium in Europe.
The Andorran bollard has an orange reflector and can also be found in Spain.
Yellow and turquoise-green traffic cones are used throughout the country.
Pedestrian signs have 8 stripes, a feature only shared with Spain in Europe.
Andorra has a high concentration of Generation 2 snow trekkers, especially on ski resorts.
Andorra la Vella is Europe's highest capital city and is recognizably surrounded by high mountains.
The Caldea tower and the sky wheel are prominent landmarks in the capital, Andorra la Vella.
Pas de la Casa is a touristy city in eastern Andorra with many shops and hotels. Due to its high altitude, the surrounding mountains are above the treeline.
